thread.text: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.

classes.title: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.label: Mark 11:4-7
precepts.why:
“Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee”. We have to believe our king is coming. He “is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.”

Mark shows the history of what Zechariah was prophesying: “And they went their way, and found the colt tied by the door without in a place where two ways met; and they loose him. And certain of them that stood there said unto them, What do ye, loosing the colt? And they said unto them even as Jesus had commanded: and they let them go. And they brought the colt to Jesus, and cast their garments on him; and he sat upon him.”

So when people say Christ isn't mentioned in the Old Testament, shut up; you don't know what you're talking about. Zechariah saw the King of Zion riding upon the colt, and Mark records Christ sitting upon that colt. He is our King, just and having salvation, and he is coming to the daughter of Zion.

precepts.label: Psalms 72:8
precepts.why:
Zechariah says the King “shall speak peace unto the heathen: and his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.” David says the same: “He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.” And he reads on: “They that dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him; and his enemies shall lick the dust.”

They are scared of the saying from the river to the sea. Well, that's in the Bible too. And it is not just that little area. It is from sea to sea, meaning the whole planet earth is ours. When we went into the land, the Lord gave us that portion according to the number of the children of Israel, but the whole earth really belongs to us, to the ends of the earth.

In that day “I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off”, meaning we would have no military during that time. The King's dominion is our defence, and his enemies shall lick the dust.

precepts.label: Hebrews 13:20
precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.” What is the blood of thy covenant? Hebrews shows it: “Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant”.

The blood of the everlasting covenant is Christ dying on the cross. By that blood God sends forth his prisoners out of the pit.

If you didn't know it, this is the pit. Like it says, yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death; Ezekiel 37 calls America the valley of dry bones. This is the pit, and “no water” means there is no truth here.

Then Zechariah says, “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”. We are the prisoners of hope, and the stronghold is the Lord, this Bible: “The Lord is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.” By Christ's blood we are brought out of the pit to the stronghold.

thread.text: Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope: even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee;

classes.title: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.label: Nahum 1:7
precepts.why:
Zechariah says “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope.” Nahum tells us what that stronghold is: “The Lord is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.” The stronghold is the Lord, and that means this Bible.

The verse before in Zechariah speaks of the pit “wherein is no water”, meaning there is no truth. That pit is America, the valley of dry bones of Ezekiel 37. Out of that pit, the prisoners are told to turn to the stronghold.

So turning to the stronghold is turning to the Lord and his word. He is good, he is our strong hold in the day of trouble, and he knows them that trust in him. We are the prisoners of hope, and the Bible calls us that.

precepts.label: Proverbs 1:23
precepts.why:
Zechariah says turn you to the stronghold; Proverbs says “Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.” God's reproof is his laws.

So there is a stipulation to get God's Holy Spirit: you must turn at God's reproof. The laws come before the spirit. Only when you turn to his laws will he pour out his spirit on you and make known his words to you.

That is why all these dumb Christians that say they have the Holy Spirit and won't keep a commandment do not have it. They have Satan on them. Turning to the stronghold, for us prisoners of hope, means turning at his reproof and keeping his laws.

precepts.label: John 14:15-18
precepts.why:
More proof that the spirit comes after the laws: Christ said the same thing. “If ye love me, keep my commandments. And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever”.

Who is that Comforter? “Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.” Then Christ says, “I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.” He is letting us know he is the Comforter. It ain't Muhammad. Christ is the Comforter; he is the Holy Spirit.

So the one who turns to the stronghold and keeps the commandments is the one who receives Christ, the Spirit of truth. Those who claim the Holy Spirit and keep no commandment do not have him.

People don't reject the truth because it is false; they reject it because it is uncomfortable. Black and Latino people hate the discomfort of change. But knowledge you won't act on just sits there and becomes nothing, like people who say they want to lose weight, know what to do, and won't do a damn thing.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:19-20
precepts.why:
Why does Zechariah call us prisoners of hope? Peter says Christ “went and preached unto the spirits in prison”. When Christ came, he preached to the spirits in prison. That's us: our mothers and fathers, our sons and daughters. We are in a spiritual prison.

When Rome was dominating us, that was a prison. We didn't have free rule; Rome was over us.

Those spirits in prison are the ones “Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.” That disobedient people is you and me. We are the prisoners, and our hope is in the stronghold.

precepts.label: Isaiah 61:1
precepts.why:
Isaiah shows what Christ was sent to do for those prisoners: “The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound”.

We are in a prison house, and we are bound in sin. Christ is anointed to proclaim liberty to us captives and to open the prison to us that are bound.

That is why we are prisoners of hope: the prison is real, but the one anointed to open it has come, and we are told to turn to him, the stronghold.

precepts.label: John 8:32-34
precepts.why:
Christ said, “And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” They answered him, “We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free?” So they knew being made free referred to being in bondage. They said, we were never slaves.

They couldn't see that Rome was over them. They were paying taxes to Rome and were oblivious to it, because they were rich and wealthy.

So watch what Christ says: “Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.” He took it down a level: you won't understand what I just said, but you are a servant. You are bound in your sins.

That is the prison of the prisoners of hope: bound under the nations and bound in sin. The truth, turning to the stronghold, is what makes us free.

precepts.label: Romans 6:12-13
precepts.why:
If sin is the prison, Paul tells us how to walk out of it: “Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.” Don't let sin reign, meaning rule, within you.

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.”

Our bodies must be vessels of righteousness, used for the commandments of God and nothing else. That is how the prisoners of hope turn to the stronghold: no longer servants of sin, but instruments of righteousness unto God.

precepts.label: Isaiah 61:7-9
precepts.why:
Zechariah says “even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”. Isaiah shows what that double is: “For your shame ye shall have double”. The shame we have suffered in captivity after captivity, we shall have double for it.

“and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion”, because we are a confused people; take a look at TikTok and Instagram. “therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them.” God says “I the Lord love judgment, I hate robbery for burnt offering; and I will direct their work in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.”

Watch the double we are going to get: “And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.” We have never experienced that. Imagine walking down the street and everybody knows your kids' names and moves the hell out of their way: that's brother so-and-so's kid. All people are going to know our children. That's double.

Write down the chain of events: awakening, which is us waking up; followed by tribulation, and we are between those now; World War III; Armageddon in the midst of that war, where Christ makes his advent; deliverance; wilderness; then kings and priests, rulership.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:4
precepts.why:
Obadiah is spoken “concerning Edom”, the same Esau that God hated in Malachi. “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” God made him low, and he hated it.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” That is the one who dwelt in the cliffs of the rocks, in the mountains: cave dwellers, Caucasians, troglodytes. He was displaced out of his land and ended up in the Caucasus Mountains, and when he gained power on the earth he said in his heart that nobody could bring him down.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle”: Greece, Rome, Spain, Portugal, they all rose up as the eagle, and America rose up as the eagle. “And though thou set thy nest among the stars”: gaining power out in space, space travel. How did he get to the stars? Because Satan gave him power to do it: technology, rockets, rocket science, nuclear bombs.

“Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” It is the same thing God said in Malachi. Edom said “we will return and build the desolate places”: the Renaissance, the rebirth, building up Europe into a superpower on the earth. “They shall build, but I will throw down”. They will rise up again in power, but the Most High himself will bring them down, and they are “the border of wickedness”, the beginning and the end of all wickedness on the earth, with his people, “against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:1
precepts.why:
Matthew writes “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”, and Isaiah had already written it: “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.”

Matthew says “Galilee of the Gentiles”; Isaiah says “Galilee of the nations.” So the nations also means the Gentiles. Same land, same people, same word.

What we read in Matthew 4:15 was already recorded in the Old Testament. When the apostles and prophets spoke, they had to substantiate their points from what we call the Old Testament today. Whatever they said, they had to be able to justify it with that text. Matthew is not saying something new; he is showing the prophecy fulfilled.

This is the foundation for Acts 10. By the biblical text the Jews were going to be dispersed among the Gentiles and live like Gentiles, like strangers, like heathens. The New Testament shows Paul going out to find them scattered among the nations and bring them back to God, because the prophecy sent from the Old Testament was that the job was to raise up the 12 tribes of Israel again. The Gentiles of Galilee are Israelites that were scattered and cut off, and God is gathering them back.

thread.label: Matthew 5:23
thread.text: Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee;

precepts.label: Matthew 8:4
precepts.why:
The heathen offered their sacrifices under every green tree and under every thick oak, where they offered sweet savour to their idols. Matthew 5 shows what a sacrifice is called: “if thou bring thy gift to the altar”, and “Leave there thy gift before the altar”, and “then come and offer thy gift”. The gift is the sacrifice.

Matthew 8 proves it again. Christ healed the leper and told him: “See thou tell no man; but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.” Moses commanded a gift, a sacrifice. The offering at the altar is called a gift.

So when the heathen sacrifice under a tree, they put gifts under the tree. You do not put gifts on top of the tree, beside the tree, or hang them on the tree. You put them under the tree. Where did you learn that from? The gifts under the Christmas tree are offerings at the heathen altar.

Isaiah 57 shows what else was under the tree: “Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children”. Those children were gifts too, slain under the tree. That is why they use the children to allure us in all the most popular holidays, Halloween and Christmas.

precepts.label: Sirach 20:29
precepts.why:
“Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise”. Why? Because you have technology. You have Google. You can easily look this up and see it is pagan. But because we are so covetous and want that self-gratification, the gifts blind us: Thanksgiving gifts, Valentine's Day gifts, New Year's gifts, Halloween gifts, Christmas gifts, the Easter suit, your Sunday finest on Easter. Always gifts.

“And stop up his mouth that he cannot reprove.” He knows it is wrong. He knows it is evil. But he will not say anything, and he will even fight for it. Many black and brown men will battle for Christmas for hours; ask one if he is married and he says yes. So you are scared to lose a vagina. Tell your wife today, babe, Christmas is pagan, we are not celebrating it no more, and she will put a lock and key on that box, and you will never see it again. The woman has got you by the balls, gift wrapped under the tree. That is the ordinance.

So the gifts under the tree are not harmless. They are the offering at the heathen altar, and they blind the eyes of the wise and stop the mouth of the man who should reprove it.

precepts.label: Acts 11:19
precepts.why:
“Go not into the way of the Gentiles”: in this verse that includes the other eleven tribes. “And into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not”: that is the Northern Kingdom. Why? Because it was not their time yet. The Lord said he would raise the tents of Judah first. “But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel”: that starts with Judah first.

Some are confused and think this is new. It is not; it has always been taught. Acts shows the order being followed after Christ: “Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.”

To none but the Jews only: only to Judah. They were primarily dealing with Judah first.

That does not mean the rest were never to be reached. Christ himself went to Samaria in John 4 and taught the Samaritans for a few days, because he knew the time was coming to deal with them. Judah first, and then the other tribes.

precepts.label: Romans 9:24
precepts.why:
The disciples went first to Judah, “preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” Then watch what Paul says: “Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?”

“Even us”: the tribe of Benjamin and all the other tribes. “Whom he hath called, not of the Jews only”: not of Judah only. “But also of the Gentiles”: the other eleven tribes.

Some were perverting Zechariah 12:7, where the Lord raises the tents of Judah first, as if it meant only Judah. Judah first is the order, not the whole. So go back to Matthew 10 with a better understanding: “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” In the beginning it was Judah first; afterward the call went to the rest of the tribes. There is no contradiction once you know the order.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:4
precepts.why:
People say the people in the land of Israel today are the Jews. That is not what the Bible says. After the tribulation, when the stars fall (the missiles) and the powers of the heavens are shaken (nations warring against each other), “he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Notice the angels do not go to one land to gather this people. Christ is letting us know the Israelites would not be in a land; they would be scattered worldwide.

Who is the elect? Some say anybody who worships. Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. That is the elect: Israel, scattered in the four winds from one end of heaven to the other.

Before the angels come for them, the Lord calls to the heavens and to the earth: “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” The saints are “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”, and only the Israelites made a covenant with God by sacrifice. The call to the heavens is to the angels; the call to the earth is to us.

So the message for us on earth is the same as the angels' commandment: gather the saints. We are not supposed to be looking for other races and nationalities, only the twelve tribes of Israel, scattered worldwide, which is why the gospel has to go out to every land.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:1-5
precepts.why:
Christ said the sun would be darkened and the stars would fall from heaven before the sign of the Son of man appears. Ezra shows the same end, and it goes into the land of Israel and those who call themselves Jews and are not being destroyed.

“The days shall come, that they which dwell upon earth shall be taken in a great number”. That is the third woe: billions of people are going to die. “And the way of truth shall be hidden”: who the Israelites are, who the people of that land are, is hidden. “And the land shall be barren of faith. But iniquity shall be increased above that which now thou seest, or that thou hast heard long ago.” You see how wicked this world is getting; that was prophesied.

“And the land, that thou seest now to have root, shalt thou see wasted suddenly.” The land that has root now is the land of Israel, and it will be destroyed suddenly by the Persians and the Arabs. That goes back to the destruction at noonday. Wasted is the word Isaiah uses: “I have created the waster to destroy.” Seeing the land wasted means nuclear bombs.

“But if the most High grant thee to live, thou shalt see after the third trumpet”: in Revelation the third trump is nuclear war. “That the sun shall suddenly shine again in the night”: a nuclear bomb going off at night looks like the sun shining. That is what the prophet saw. “And the moon thrice in the day”: three bombs going off in the day, at Ekron, Ashdod and Ashkelon. “And blood shall drop out of wood”.

That is why Iran was attacked: they are trying to stop prophecy, or slow it down. But God's counsel shall stand. Iran will develop nuclear warheads, the Arabs will unite, and they will be brought down in the valley of Jehoshaphat. The day of the Lord will not come on us as a thief, because we are watching the signs.

precepts.label: Psalms 35:1
precepts.why:
Christ said, “Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.” You don't know when the time is coming, so you need to stay prepared, stay ready. The prophecy is unfolding before our eyes: the ten horns giving their kingdoms to the beast, NATO sending weapons and troops here and there, and a time coming when those horns will hate the whore.

So what do we pray for? David shows us: “Plead my cause, O Lord, with them that strive with me: fight against them that fight against me.” Watch and pray for protection and deliverance, asking the Lord to fight against them that fight against us.

Watch and pray that none of us drift, get isolated, or get taken by sin and deception. You can pray for that. These Black Christians don't know what to pray for, but the scripture shows you: pray for the Lord to plead our cause against them that strive with us.

precepts.label: Luke 21:36
precepts.why:
“Take ye heed, watch and pray”, and Christ tells us what to watch and pray for: “Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.”

Watch and pray for the destruction of their wicked devices: that the traps, the plots and the lies of the enemy be exposed and broken. Ask the Most High to show you.

Pray for prophecy to be fulfilled. And pray that you are worthy to stand before Christ when these things come. We see all this unfolding, the nations moving and the empire declining, so the prayer is not for these things to be stopped but for us to be found worthy to escape them and stand before the Son of man.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 4:7-8
precepts.why:
Christ said to watch and pray, “for ye know not when the time is.” Peter says the same: “But the end of all things is at hand: be ye therefore sober, and watch unto prayer.” Be sober, man. Keep a clear mind.

“And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.” Fervent charity is the brotherly love we are supposed to have for one another, the way we are supposed to treat one another.

We need it because these things are taking place, and we see them taking place on the earth. The end of all things is at hand, so watching and praying goes together with a clear mind and with love among ourselves.

precepts.label: Colossians 4:2
precepts.why:
Watching and praying is not only for the nation at large. “Continue in prayer, and watch in the same with thanksgiving”. Watch and pray for your household, your children, your brothers and sisters, because if the house fails, the nation gets weaker.

That is why marriage classes keep coming up. The scripture says it is not good for man to be alone. Some brothers think they are strong enough to do it without her, but it is not good that you should be alone; two are better than one.

And watch in the same with thanksgiving: be thankful for the things you have right now, because some people are in a way worse position than you. So continue in prayer, be thankful, and keep preparing, because you do not know when the time is.

precepts.label: John 4:19-22
precepts.why:
Christ told the Samaritan woman by the well the same thing he said in Luke 21. She said, “Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet. Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.” The Samaritans worshipped up on Mount Gerizim, because their fathers used to worship up there back in the days.

“Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Ye worship ye know not what”. The Samaritans were not going to worship in that mountain, and the Jews, the Israelites, would not be worshipping at Jerusalem either.

What is Christ saying here? What Luke 21 says: we would “fall by the edge of the sword”, and be “led away captive into all nations”, carried away as slaves into all nations. We fell by the sword in 70 AD, and being led into all nations is a process of time; it didn't all happen in 70 AD. Jerusalem would be “trodden down of the Gentiles”, occupied by heathens, until Christ returns and destroys the Gentiles.

In 70 AD most of us fled into Africa, formed communities, built cities and mingled amongst the Hamitic tribes. Esau drew maps pinpointing where the tribes were all over Africa, the Levite cities of Nigeria, Bnei Ephraim on the slave coast, the Jewish kingdoms, because slavery was not coincidence. Slavery was war.

precepts.label: Hosea 4:17
precepts.why:
The woman of Samaria said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” These Samaritans were Israelites who still lived there. Samaria is north of Jerusalem, as the map shows, and the Jews of Jerusalem stopped dealing with our people located in Samaria.

Why did that happen? A brother answered from Hosea: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” That is why she said it. The scripture said Ephraim was joined to idols, and the word was to let him alone.

So the separation between the Jews and the Samaritans was not just a grudge; it grew out of the judgment on the northern kingdom for its idolatry. Judah took that word and left Ephraim alone. Yet here Christ, of Judah, sits at Jacob's well and asks a woman of Samaria to give him drink.

precepts.label: Hosea 1:6-11
precepts.why:
Hosea shows why Ephraim was let alone. “Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.” He would no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, because they fully went into idolatry. “But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen”, as can be read in 2 Kings 19.

“Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” That was the message to the northern kingdom because of his anger at their idolatry: you will not be my people, and I will not be your God. That is why the woman said the Jews have no dealings with us.

But then it comes back: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” What is he saying? I am going to bring you back together again.

All the prophets spoke from a place of prophecy, judgment, and eventually redemption. That is what gives us hope to change and repent. If there were no endgame where we come out of this, there would be no incentive. But God said if you turn back to me, in the place where it was said you are not my people, there you will be called the sons of God.

precepts.label: Isaiah 7:8
precepts.why:
Before Hosea recorded the Lord casting off the house of Israel, Isaiah had already prophesied it: “For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.”

They already knew. God already told them that within sixty-five years Ephraim, the northern kingdom, would be broken and destroyed, and that is what Hosea 1 is recording: Lo–ruhamah, no more mercy on the house of Israel, and Lo–ammi, ye are not my people.

So when the woman of Samaria says the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans, she is standing at the end of that prophecy. Ephraim was broken “that it be not a people”, cut off for idolatry. And that is exactly why it matters that Christ, a Jew, is speaking to her at Jacob's well: the people who were broken off are about to be offered the living water.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:26
precepts.why:
Christ told her, “If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.” What is the living water? A brother answered from Ephesians: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”.

You are cleansed by the washing of water by the word, so the living water is the word of God. What Christ would have given her was understanding: the understanding that the tribes were going to be gathered back together again.

She said, “Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well”? That shows she understood she was part of the twelve tribes of Israel; she just knew the Jews had no dealings with them. And Christ answered, “Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst”. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they had been disconnected from it for so long.

precepts.label: Colossians 1:23-29
precepts.why:
The water Christ gives is “a well of water springing up into everlasting life”, and Paul shows what that understanding is. He is a minister of the gospel “which was preached to every creature which is under heaven”, to fulfil the word of God: “Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints”.

It was hid for ages that the northern kingdom had a part to play in this, to repent and come back. The ones who did understand were the learned men who studied, many of them the Pharisees, which is why they said, will he go to the dispersed among the Gentiles and teach them? They read Isaiah, Ezekiel and Deuteronomy. The masses didn't have the scriptures; the learned men had the parchment. But now he gave it to the apostles to teach.

“To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory”. The riches of this mystery among the Gentiles is that the northern kingdom has an opportunity of repentance: he is gathering back the Gentiles. The secret hid for ages is being revealed to the whole world; it is no longer gatekept. The apostles would go throughout the earth and teach the people that you are not Puerto Rican, you are not Dominican, whatever byword was given to you: you are the children of Israel. “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom”.

That is what is happening to us now. The understanding of this Bible and of who we are was hid for ages, but the Lord said in this hour the true worshippers are going to wake up.

precepts.label: Joshua 8:30-35
precepts.why:
The woman at the well said, “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. On the map, the mountains above the well are Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. Joshua 8 shows why she said it: “Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, “an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron: and they offered thereon burnt offerings unto the Lord, and sacrificed peace offerings.” “And he wrote there upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel.”

When we first came into the land, the first place we came into was what would be called Samaria, and the first altars were set up in Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. That is why, when the nation split, the northern kingdom went back up top and worshipped there: this is the place where we worshipped initially. But God called his home Jerusalem; that is where he set up his temple.

Read on: “And all Israel, and their elders, and officers, and their judges, stood on this side the ark and on that side before the priests the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, as well the stranger, as he that was born among them; half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”. The blessings went up on the children of Israel, and the cursing was on Mount Ebal.

“There was not a word of all that Moses commanded, which Joshua read not before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them.” When we came into the land we had a mixed multitude of the other nations among us, and they were conversant in the laws of God. They had to learn the laws. We taught them how to keep the Sabbath day: six days you do your work, and on the seventh no work, neither your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor the stranger that is within thy gates.

Then Christ answered her: “Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” There was a time coming, 70 AD, when Jerusalem would be toppled by the Romans, and neither the mountains of Samaria nor Jerusalem would matter, because he was destroying it. His purpose was to gather in one the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.label: Acts 17:11
precepts.why:
“Search the scriptures.” Our job is to search the scriptures. The nations don't; they leave their scripture searching to Matthew through Revelation with their misunderstanding from Christianity. If you start from Genesis, you find out that salvation and rulership of the earth is only for the Israelites through Christ. The Bereans show how it is done: “These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.”

When Paul presented the truth of Christ to them, they did not just take it; they searched the scriptures daily to see whether what Paul was teaching was accurate according to the scriptures. That is what made them more noble, and that is what we have to do.

The scriptures they searched were the same ones Christ said “testify of me.” Searching them daily with a ready mind is how the truth of Christ is proved.

precepts.label: Proverbs 25:2
precepts.why:
“It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.” When God conceals something, it is in parable form, metaphors and allegories, and it is our job to figure out what the Lord means by A, B and C.

That is why we must search. Read Jeremiah 48, “against Moab”, or Jeremiah 49, “Concerning the Ammonites”, and unless you search the scriptures and pray to the Lord, you'll say, I don't know who Moab is, I don't know who the Ammonites are, I don't know who Gad is, I'm confused, so I'll stick to Matthew through Revelation. That's what the churches do. Christians don't know and Muslims don't know, confused and discombobulated, unable to identify these nations today.

The honour of kings is to search it out: to find who Moab, Ammon, Gad and Asia are today. The matter is concealed, but it is there for those who search.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 29:29
precepts.why:
“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.”

What God has kept secret and then revealed to us is for our children and our children's children forever. So what we bring out in the scriptures is meant for our sons and our daughters. Teach them. Don't let this truth fall by the wayside, with your sons and daughters worshipping Caesar Borgia all over again. That would be a detriment to you and your family.

Searching the scriptures is not only for ourselves. What the Lord reveals by it belongs to us and to our children, so that we and they may do all the words of this law.

precepts.label: John 5:30
precepts.why:
“Yet a little while am I with you, and then I go unto him that sent me.” Who sent Jesus? Christ answers it himself: “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

He did not come on his own errand. He was sent from his Father, and he sought only the Father's will. And that will was to gather the twelve tribes of Israel: other sheep he must bring in, that there might be one fold and one shepherd. The gathering began when Christ came and began to teach, and his death was the beginning of the twelve tribes being brought back together.

So when he says he goes “unto him that sent me”, he is going back to the Father whose will he came to do. What that will was, the prophets had already written, and Isaiah 11 shows it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:1-3
precepts.why:
The Old Testament shows who was sent and why. “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”: that Branch is Christ, as Zechariah 6 shows. “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.”

Then: “and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears.” That is the same exact thing Christ said in John 5:30: “as I hear, I judge”, “I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” The Branch out of Jesse does not judge by himself; he does the will of the one who sent him.

So what did God send him to do? Keep reading in the same chapter, and verse 12 tells it: to set up an ensign, assemble the outcasts of Israel and gather the dispersed of Judah. When Christ spoke in the New Testament, he was reiterating what the Old Testament already said, and the text substantiates it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:10-12
precepts.why:
“And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.” Who are the Gentiles here? The Jews in John 7 asked, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The answer is Israel, and it is proven by staying in the passage.

“the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The Gentiles that seek the root of Jesse are the outcasts of Israel, the remnant of his people.

That was God's will in sending his Son: to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. The Pharisees and chief priests were studied men. They understood this prophecy of the dispersed, which is why they asked whether he would go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles.

precepts.label: Proverbs 1:27-28
precepts.why:
“Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, thither ye cannot come.” The Old Testament already spoke it: “When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you. Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me.”

They will not. The same words Christ spoke to the Pharisees and chief priests are written in Proverbs, against those who would not hear. When Christ, the apostles and the prophets spoke in the New Testament, their conversation was reiterating what the Old Testament was saying, and they could substantiate it with the text.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:64
precepts.why:
Isaiah 11 says “he shall set up an ensign for the nations”. Why for the nations? Because Israel was going to be scattered: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

We were going to be scattered in all these nations and live as Gentiles, serving other gods. So the ensign set up for the nations is set up to “assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The ones he gathers out of the nations are Israel.

That is what the Jews meant in John 7 when they asked, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles”? They knew the curse: Israel scattered from one end of the earth to the other.

precepts.label: Tobit 3:4
precepts.why:
Tobit shows the dispersed are Israel once again: “For they obeyed not thy commandments: wherefore thou hast delivered us for a spoil, and unto captivity, and unto death, and for a proverb of reproach to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.”

Israel disobeyed the commandments, and so was delivered for a spoil, into captivity, unto death, and made a proverb of reproach among all the nations where they were dispersed. The Pharisees understood Tobit and the dispersed, just as they understood Isaiah 11. That is why they said of Christ, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” They knew who the dispersed were.

precepts.label: Tobit 13:5
precepts.why:
“And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he hath scattered us.” Again it uses the word nations, explaining that it was Israel being scattered among them.

The scourge is for our iniquities, but mercy comes again, and the promise is the gathering out of all nations. That is the same gathering Isaiah 11 speaks of, and the same work Christ was sent to begin: bringing the dispersed out from among the Gentiles, where they had been scattered.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 36:19
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says the same: “And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries: according to their way and according to their doings I judged them.”

They're dispersed. Israel was scattered among the heathen and dispersed through the countries, judged according to their own ways and doings. The Pharisees and chief priests understood Ezekiel 36 and the dispersed, along with Isaiah 11 and Tobit 3. So when they asked, “Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?”, they were speaking of scattered Israel living among the heathen.

precepts.label: Acts 21:21
precepts.why:
The New Testament shows the dispersed being taught: “And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.” There were Jews among the Gentiles, and Paul was going to them.

We know from the text that the Jews were going to be dispersed among the Gentiles and live like Gentiles. Coming back to the New Testament, it shows Paul going out to find the Jews scattered among these other nations, living like Gentiles, living like strangers, living like heathens, and bringing them back to God.

This was the prophecy sent from the Old Testament: the job was to raise up the twelve tribes of Israel again. What the Jews in John 7 asked, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles”?, is exactly what was done.

precepts.label: Psalms 95:1-7
precepts.why:
Everything Christ and the apostles spoke was already spoken in what we call the Old Testament, and they used it to substantiate their points. So when Christ says of his other sheep, “they shall hear my voice”, the psalm already said it.

“O come, let us sing unto the Lord: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation.” The rock of our salvation is Christ. “For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. In his hand are the deep places of the earth”; “The sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the Lord our maker.”

“For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice.” We are the sheep of his hand, and the condition is the same: if you will hear his voice. That is exactly what Christ said in John 10: “them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice.”

For all of us there was a time that we heard this voice. We heard the word of God, and it brought us to repentance, to change. Something innate in us made us acknowledge the word of God by hearing his voice and changing our life. That is how the sheep of his pasture are known.

precepts.label: Micah 2:12
precepts.why:
Christ said, “there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.” The fold he was speaking in was the Jews in Jerusalem, primarily Judah, Benjamin and Levi. The other sheep, not of that fold, were the rest of Israel, and he would gather the two nations, the southern and northern kingdoms, together under one shepherd, Jesus Christ.

Micah prophesied that one fold: “I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men.”

“all of thee” means all twelve tribes. That is the same thing Christ was saying: I have sheep that are not of this fold; them also I must bring, that there may be one fold and one shepherd. The prophecy was that all twelve tribes were going to be brought back together.

The beginning of it coming to fruition was when Christ came and began to teach, and his dying was the beginning of the twelve tribes being gathered back together. That is what his death was about: he was sent by his Father to gather the flock of Jacob into one fold.

precepts.label: John 14:15
precepts.why:
The Comforter, the Holy Ghost, “shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.” Why would we need to remember the things Christ said? Because we would be made to forget. Through slavery the nations annihilated our twelve tribes, burned our records and beat us into submission, and we forgot what Christ said.

What did he say? That he would gather his elect from the four corners of the earth. That he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.”

The Holy Spirit causes us to remember these things. If you don't remember them, you don't have the Holy Spirit on you. Keeping the commandments is the love Christ asks for, and the Spirit brings back to our remembrance who we are and what he said.

That is what is happening now: brothers and sisters waking up worldwide. Isaiah 44 promised it to Jacob, whom the Lord chose: “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty”, the word upon those thirsty for the truth, and “I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring: And they shall spring up as among the grass”. The Israelites are springing up worldwide like grass.

precepts.label: Acts 4:31
precepts.why:
On the day of Pentecost “suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting”, and “they were all filled with the Holy Ghost.” That Holy Ghost was the mighty wind that filled them.

Acts 4 shows the same thing again: “And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together; and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness.” The place shook, the Holy Ghost filled them, and the result was boldness.

When the apostles spoke and the Holy Ghost filled them, they were bold in what they said, because they knew what they were saying was sent of God, and they could prove it from the scriptures. That is the spirit that came on them at Pentecost: not a show, but a boldness to speak the word of God, grounded in knowing it.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 48:12-13
precepts.why:
The Holy Ghost came at Pentecost as a rushing mighty wind. Sirach tells of another man covered by the wind: “Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: whilst he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince, neither could any bring him into subjection.”

Look what it says next: “No word could overcome him; and after his death his body prophesied.” While the spirit of God was on him, no word could overcome him.

Men, study. When you are out in the street, there should be no word that can confound you. We should not be hearing men teaching who cannot explain basic scriptures. We are going up against, for the most part, Christians, and they don't know the Bible. We should know who we are and how to explain it: Galatians 3, Ephesians 2:11-16. This is very elementary.

When the spirit of God is on you, no word should be able to overcome you. That is what filled the apostles at Pentecost, and that is what should fill the men who go out to teach today.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 37:9-10
precepts.why:
At Pentecost the Holy Ghost came as a wind. Ezekiel was told to prophesy to the wind: “Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord God; Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live.” That is the word of God coming upon them.

“So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.”

That is what was happening in Acts. They taught, and the people came in and gathered: devout men out of every nation under heaven, the scattered of Israel, hearing the word in their own tongues and standing up again.

All of you are here because the word of God was breathed on you, and it wasn't because the people teaching were shaky. So for you men out there teaching: study to shew thyself approved. The breath that raises the slain into an exceeding great army comes through a word that is taught with power.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:3
precepts.why:
At Pentecost they “began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.” Other tongues means other languages. The psalm already said it: “There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.”

There is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard. The devout men dwelling at Jerusalem came “out of every nation under heaven”, because according to Deuteronomy 28 we were going to be scattered into all nations. Every man heard the apostles speak in his own language, and they marvelled, “are not all these which speak Galileans?” That is because we were scattered among the heathen and learned their languages.

So God made sure the word reached every one of them in the tongue wherein they were born. In every language the scattered people of Israel had taken on, their voice was heard, and the gathering of the twelve tribes began.

precepts.label: Amos 5:26
precepts.why:
The Iranians burned large statues of a horned, bull-headed figure bearing the so-called Star of David, and they knew what they were doing: they were burning statues of Baal. That is not the Star of David. You cannot find it anywhere in the Bible; it is a sign in the occult.

Stephen said, “Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.” If you didn't know, Moloch is Baal: the same thing, both the devil. The star is the star of their god, the devil, Baal or Moloch.

Stephen was quoting Amos: “But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.” Which ye made to yourselves: it is idolatry. God did not give us that star. When King Solomon was dabbling in witchcraft, that is how he got that star; God never gave it to us.

So the star so-called Israel and America carry is the star of Baal, and Baal worship shows up in plain sight: the bull's head statue at the 1933 Chicago World's Fair on Jewish Day, the giant mechanical bull at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, the bull on Wall Street. Even bullheaded, stupidly stubborn, comes from Baal worship, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. That idolatry is why Israel was carried away, and why we are in captivity today.

precepts.label: Acts 22:12
precepts.why:
Cornelius is called “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house”. What does it mean to be devout? Acts 22 shows it: “And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there”. To be devout is to be devout according to the law, and to have a good report for it.

So when Acts 10 says Cornelius was a devout man, it is saying he was a law-abiding man. He kept the laws of God. He feared God with all his house, gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.

His own messengers tell Peter the same thing later in the chapter: “Cornelius the centurion, a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews”. The same good report Ananias had among the Jews, Cornelius had too.

That is why Peter came to understand that the vision was about man, not food, and that he should not call any man common or unclean. Cornelius was a just man and a devout man, a keeper of the law. “God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.”

precepts.label: Tobit 12:15
precepts.why:
The angel tells Cornelius, “Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.” How do prayers come up before God? Tobit shows it. The angel Raphael says, “I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.”

These are the angels that bring your prayers before the Most High God. Cornelius saw “an angel of God coming in to him” about the ninth hour, and that angel came because his prayers had gone up and been presented before the Holy One.

So when Acts 10 says his prayers and alms came up “for a memorial before God”, it is speaking of this very thing: the holy angels going in and out before the glory of God, presenting the prayers of those who fear him.

And the answer came back down by the same way. The angel told Cornelius to send men to Joppa and call for Simon, whose surname is Peter, who would tell him what he ought to do.

precepts.label: Tobit 12:8
precepts.why:
In the same chapter where Raphael says he presents the prayers of the saints, he says what makes those prayers go up: “Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness.” Prayer joined with fasting and alms and being righteous is what makes your prayers go before the Lord.

In other words, when you pray to God and combine it with alms and fasting, the prayers are heard before the Most High. That is exactly what we read of Cornelius in Acts 10:2: “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.”

And it is exactly what the angel told him in Acts 10:4: “Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.” Not his prayers alone, but his prayers and his alms together, from a devout man who kept the law.

So Cornelius is the example of what Tobit teaches. His righteousness, his alms and his praying alway went up before God, and God answered by sending him to Peter.

precepts.label: Hosea 12:10
precepts.why:
Peter fell into a trance and saw a vessel full of “fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air”, and a voice said, “Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.” Peter answered, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.” But the vision was not really talking about food. That is why it says “Peter doubted in himself what this vision which he had seen should mean”.

When visions come from God, they are an allegory, referring to something else many times. The Lord proves it himself: “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” A similitude shows you one thing, but it is really something else he is trying to explain.

That is what Peter was pondering. Is the Lord telling me to eat unlawful animals? No, Lord, I have never eaten anything unlawful. The beasts in the sheet were a similitude, and Peter did not yet know what they stood for.

He found out when he came to Cornelius. He said, “God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” The vision was not about unclean animals; it was about man. Cornelius was a just man and a devout man, and the vision was showing Peter that God is no respecter of persons, northern kingdom or southern kingdom: “in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” Israel, the ones called not God’s people, would one day be joined back in.

thread.label: Acts 10:11-12, the vessel decoded
thread.text: And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth:

classes.title: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common
Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.label: Hosea 8:8
precepts.why:
Peter “saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners.” Now the scriptures substantiate the vision he had. What is the vessel? Hosea says: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.”

Israel was that vessel, a vessel among the Gentiles in which nobody had pleasure. Swallowed up among the nations, Israel was not wanted by anyone.

This is why the nations cannot handle us right now: when we speak, we can use the Bible to explain itself. When they hear Acts 10, they think it is everybody. No. God said Israel was the vessel. Peter's vision was not about the whole world coming in; it was about the scattered house of Israel, living among the Gentiles, being let down before him so that it could be gathered.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:12
precepts.why:
The vessel in Peter's vision was “knit at the four corners.” The four corners are in the prophets too: “And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.”

So what is in that sheet, gathered at the four corners? It was Israel, scattered through the four corners of the earth, living as beasts. The outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah are the ones God assembles from those four corners.

He sets up an ensign “for the nations” because Israel would be scattered among all the nations and live as Gentiles. The picture of a sheet knit at four corners is the picture of God drawing his scattered people together from every end of the earth, and that is the vision Peter had to explain to those of the circumcision.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 8:29
precepts.why:
In the vessel were “all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.” Peter had to explain to the circumcision, who contended with him, that the fourfooted beasts, the wild beasts, the creeping things and the fowls of the air refer to man. So there had to be scripture to prove it.

Ezra prays: “Let it not be thy will to destroy them which have lived like beasts; but to look upon them that have clearly taught thy law.” There are men who have lived like beasts, and Ezra pleads with God not to destroy them. So we know the beast refers to man.

The vision was not about animals; it was about men. Israel, scattered and living like beasts without the law, is what was let down in that sheet, and Ezra's prayer is that God would spare them and look upon those who teach his law.

precepts.label: Psalms 73:22
precepts.why:
Another witness that the beasts in Peter's sheet are men: the psalmist says of himself, “So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee.”

A man, foolish and ignorant before God, is called a beast. So when Peter explained the vision to those of the circumcision who contended with him, he could say: remember, it is written in Psalms that we were as beasts before God.

That is the whole key to Acts 10. The fourfooted beasts in the vessel are not pork and shellfish made clean. They are the people of Israel who were foolish and ignorant, living as beasts before the Lord, whom God was now going to cleanse and gather back together.

precepts.label: Isaiah 51:20
precepts.why:
The vessel also held “wild beasts.” Isaiah names them: “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God.”

The sons of Israel, fainted and lying at the head of every street, are compared to a wild bull caught in a net, full of the fury of the Lord. The wild beast is a man of Israel under God's rebuke.

When Peter explained the fourfooted beasts and wild beasts, he would have to refer to scriptures like these. Remember, it is written in 2 Esdras that we lived as beasts. Remember, it is written in Psalms that we were as beasts. Remember, Isaiah the prophet said we would be as a wild bull. The vision was about men, and the scriptures prove it.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 1:14
precepts.why:
The vessel also held “creeping things.” Who are the creeping things? The vision was not about animals; it was about man, so there has to be a scripture showing that the creeping thing refers to man. Habakkuk says to God: “And makest men as the fishes of the sea, as the creeping things, that have no ruler over them?”

Men made as creeping things that have no ruler over them. When we were without God, with no ruler, we were like creeping things, like insects or bugs. Without the laws of God, we were like beasts, like animals.

So every creature in Peter's sheet is a description of Israel scattered without God and without his law. The creeping things are men with no ruler over them, and God was about to bring them back under his rule.

precepts.label: Hosea 7:11-12
precepts.why:
The last creatures in the vessel are the “fowls of the air.” There had to be scripture to show that the fowls of the air also refer to man. Hosea says: “Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria. When they shall go, I will spread my net upon them; I will bring them down as the fowls of the heaven; I will chastise them, as their congregation hath heard.”

Ephraim, the northern kingdom, is the silly dove, brought down as the fowls of the heaven. So the fowls in Peter's vision are Israelites too.

Now imagine those of the circumcision hearing Peter speak: listen, over here in Hosea, remember, God called us fowls. God was showing him it was time to gather the twelve tribes, north and south, back together.

That is why the scripture says prove all things. Everything must be proven as it is written, that thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and overcome when thou art judged. Peter did not just tell a vision; he could prove every creature in it from the prophets.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 37:22
precepts.why:
Peter says, “Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation”. That phrase “another nation” might throw you off, because Christians use it to say Peter was going to other races. Ezekiel shows what that other nation is: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

The kingdom of Judah was called a nation, and the kingdom of Israel, Ephraim and the rest, was called a nation. Two nations, two separate kingdoms, but one people. So when Peter the Jew, of Judah, speaks of coming unto one of another nation, that other nation is the kingdom of Israel, the northern kingdom. That is what the vision of the sheet was about: “God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean”, speaking of Cornelius and his family.

Then Peter says God “is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” A Christian will stop you right there, but read the next verse: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ”. That tells you who Cornelius and his kinfolk were: the children of Israel, scattered in every nation.

Acts 15 looks back on this and quotes the prophets: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”. The regathering of the twelve tribes, the two kingdoms coming back together, is what Acts 10 is about. God is bringing the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom back into one nation, just as Ezekiel said.

thread.label: Acts 10:13, rise, kill, and eat
thread.text: And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.

classes.title: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.label: Baruch 5:5
precepts.why:
We know now the vision is referring to man. So what is the “Rise” talking about? What was the whole purpose of the vision? To gather the northern and southern kingdoms back together, to gather us back from where we were scattered, east to west, north and south.

Baruch uses the same word: “Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold thy children gathered from the west unto the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God.” The children are coming from the west unto the east, and they rejoice when they remember God.

They are gathered “by the word of the Holy One.” That word is what is going to gather the children of Israel back together. This is it right here.

So when the voice says “Rise, Peter”, he is telling Peter: it is time. Awake. Rise. Now it is time to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. The arising comes first; then comes the kill and the eat, because before we gather the twelve tribes we first have to be made ready to teach them.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 8:12
precepts.why:
“Rise, Peter; kill”. What does kill mean? A brother answered: kill the old man, the old mindset, as it is written in Romans 6. That is right. But in that time there was no New Testament. Peter would have to explain it to those of the circumcision using the Old Testament.

Ezra gives it: “Thou broughtest it up with thy righteousness, and nurturedst it in thy law, and reformedst it with thy judgment. And thou shalt mortify it as thy creature, and quicken it as thy work.” That is what you do. You have to mortify, deaden, kill the old man, and be quickened as God’s work.

That is the “kill” in Peter’s vision. Rise, Peter, and kill the old man. Mortify yourself. Discipline yourself. The man God brings up in his righteousness, nurtures in his law and reforms with his judgment is the man who has put the old man to death.

Only after the old man is killed can you eat, learn the scripture, and then go out and teach. That is the order God gave Peter before sending him to gather the northern kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 8:4-5
precepts.why:
After “kill” comes “eat”. What does eat mean? Learn the scripture. Ezra says it plainly: “Swallow then down, O my soul, understanding, and devour wisdom.” That is the eating. You have to go out and learn.

And after you learn, what do you do? “For thou hast agreed to give ear, and art willing to prophesy: for thou hast no longer space than only to live.” You gave ear, you devoured wisdom, and now you are willing to prophesy. After you learn, you go out and prophesy.

So the whole vision is laid out. Rise, Peter: it is time to gather the twelve tribes of Israel back together. Kill, Peter: kill the old man, mortify yourself. Eat, Peter: devour wisdom. Then go out and prophesy.

This is the Old Testament way Peter would have explained it to those of the circumcision: the eating in the vision was never about unclean beasts, but about swallowing down understanding so he could teach the scattered of Israel.

precepts.label: Revelation 10:9-11
precepts.why:
Revelation says the same thing. John went to the angel and said, “Give me the little book. And he said unto me, Take it, and eat it up; and it shall make thy belly bitter, but it shall be in thy mouth sweet as honey.” John “took the little book out of the angel’s hand, and ate it up”, and it was sweet as honey in his mouth, and as soon as he had eaten it his belly was bitter.

Then comes the reason for the eating: “Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.” The book is eaten so that it can be prophesied.

That is the same pattern as “Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.” You have to eat, you have to learn, and then you must go out and prophesy. John ate the book and was sent before many peoples and nations; Peter was told to eat and was sent to the house of Cornelius.

So eating in the vision means taking in the word. Rise, kill the old man, eat the word, and go out and prophesy to the scattered tribes.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 6:1
precepts.why:
Peter answered the vision, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.” To understand what he meant by common, go to Solomon: “There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men”.

Common is tied to evil. Peter understood that. So when he said he had never eaten anything common, he was not only talking about meat. In other words: I have never done sin, I have never dealt with sin, I have never dealt with people that were evil.

That is why the vision had to be explained to him. The sheet let down from heaven was not about food; it was about men, and Peter was being told to go among people he had counted as common.

precepts.label: Baruch 6:11
precepts.why:
Baruch shows the word common used again for evil. Speaking of the idolaters and their gods, “they will give thereof to the common harlots, and deck them as men with garments, being gods of silver, and gods of gold, and wood.” The common harlots: the word goes with whoredom and idolatry.

So when Peter said, “I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean”, he was saying, I have never dealt with sinners. I have never sat down with them.

But then the voice spake unto him again the second time, “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.” What had God cleansed? The subject matter is man. And to explain that cleansing to those of the circumcision, Peter would have to go to the Old Testament: to Ezekiel 37, where God would save them out of their dwelling places and cleanse them, take the children of Israel from among the heathen and make two kingdoms one; and to Hosea 1, where in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, it would be said, Ye are the sons of the living God.

The time had come to gather the northern kingdom back together. And that is happening now: God's people are being gathered in South America, in Africa and here in the States.

When Paul came preaching Christ, “many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds”, and those who used curious arts brought their books of witchcraft together and burned them before all men, fifty thousand pieces of silver worth. “So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.”

That is what stirred the city. Then verse 24: “For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets”. The head of Christ is the false Christ. The false prophets are the missionaries, the Jesuits, the Christian pastors and ministers, the Catholic priests and popes.

They “shall shew great signs and wonders”: the technology. Christian America created great wonders, nuclear war, fire falling down from heaven, the same wonders John mentioned in Revelation. “insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.” It is not possible, but his technological advancements, turning a man to a woman and a woman to a man, his science, cars, televisions and phones, make him a god to our people, as if no one is better than him.

That is why God says “Learn not the way of the heathen”. Our people follow his traditions to the death, but his Jesus is another Jesus, and his gospel is another gospel.

precepts.label: John 7:35
precepts.why:
Paul keeps saying “among”: the gospel “which I preach among the Gentiles”, preaching him “among the heathen”. Why does he keep using that word? Because Israel was scattered among the nations, and that is who he is writing to the entire time. Then he says “the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter”. Christ wrought effectually in Peter toward the Jews born and raised in the law and circumcised the eighth day, “the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles”.

Who are those Gentiles? John answers: “Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The Jews here are the circumcision, born and raised in the Mosaic law. They ask where Christ will go that they cannot find him. Will he go to the dispersed? The dispersed are the Israelites, the diaspora scattered among the Gentiles.

And what do the Jews call those dispersed Israelites? Gentiles: “and teach the Gentiles”. So now you know who the Gentiles are that Paul writes to throughout the entire time. It should be a no-brainer now.

That is why James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, “that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision”: Paul to the Israelites scattered among the nations, the others to the Jews who were not scattered abroad. And it is why Paul withstood Peter at Antioch. Peter ate with these Gentiles, the scattered Israelites he was teaching who they are, then withdrew when certain came from James, fearing them of the circumcision. You cannot teach the scattered who they are and then act as if you are not with them; that is a bad example.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 1:22
precepts.why:
James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, “that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.” The heathen are the northern kingdom. Peter already knew this. God had shown him that he could not call any man common or unclean. He sat with them, and he convinced many of the Jews that these men were all right, that God had granted them repentance unto life too.

“But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.” When certain came from James, Peter “withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.” Dissimulation means deception, hypocrisy, pretence, deceit, fakery: in other words, being fake. Paul said to him before them all, you are being fake like they were fake. Peter knew better, and he was corrected in front of everybody. He would have been embarrassed and ashamed.

But he repented. And as a teacher, what do you teach after that? What you repented from: do not be fake. So Peter wrote “Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently”.

Peter came back and taught it after he learned it: I was wrong. We cannot have fake love for the brethren, because God already showed me, and when I was put to the test I was influenced not to accept them. So the message now is, do not have feigned love for the brethren.

precepts.label: Acts 3:24-26
precepts.why:
“And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.” The heathen are the Gentiles: the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, justified through faith. But Christians say, see, brother, all nations will be blessed. So what does it mean?

Peter answers: “Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days.” They foretold, as Paul says the scripture foresaw. “Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers”. The ye are the Israelites. Abraham was a prophet, and the covenant passed from Abraham to Isaac to Jacob, “saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.”

“Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities.” Unto you first, the Israelites. The blessing is Christ dying for the Israelites, for all of us scattered among all the nations. The earth is too big for us to reach all our people, but Christ's blood covers us wherever we are found. That is how all the kindreds of the earth are blessed: Israel scattered among those nations and blessed with the death of Christ.

And Esau? He already got his blessing: blood and death, slavery, weaponry, war, bloodshed, nukes and witchcraft. He is literally dropping those blessings on Iran right now. He does not need any more. The other nations' blessing is to work, to build up our kingdom, and to survive the destruction as servants. “So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:25
precepts.why:
“foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith”. How do we know who is justified? You will not find anywhere in the law and the prophets that Christ was going to justify, atone for or reconcile all the heathen Gentile nations through his death. What you find is this: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

All the seed of Israel, all the families scattered abroad over the earth, justified by faith in Christ. Whether they are called Jews or called Gentiles, they shall be justified, because Christ died for them among the nations.

Now show me a precept where all the seed of Edom will be justified. All the seed of Moab justified. All the seed of Ishmael, all the seed of the Canaanites. Show me one place. It is nowhere in there.

So “they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham”: the Israelites who have faith in Christ are the children of Abraham, known for his strong faith. Abraham believed God first, and only afterward offered sacrifices, and his faith, not the animal, was counted for righteousness. That is how the seed of Israel is justified, and why “they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.”
